title: Japanese proper prime quotients make finite-extension normalizations Noetherian
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with fraction field $K$. Suppose that $R/\mathfrak q$ is Japanese (N-2) [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] for every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset R$. For every finite field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension], the integral closure $T$ of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a Noetherian ring. No separability of $L/K$ or normality of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Marot, Sur les anneaux universellement japonais (1975), Lemma 1.2, printed pp.104-105, with the stronger hypothesis on all nonzero primes used in Proposition 2.3, printed p.107.

proof.text: Choose a $K$-basis $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of $L$. Each $x_i$ satisfies a monic equation $X^{m_i}+\sum_{j<m_i}c_{ij}X^j=0$ over $K$, since its powers are linearly dependent. Choose $0\ne a_i\in R$ clearing all coefficient denominators. Then $y_i=a_ix_i$ satisfies the monic equation $Y^{m_i}+\sum_{j<m_i}a_i^{m_i-j}c_{ij}Y^j=0$ over $R$. Thus $y_i\in T$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. By [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring], $B=R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\subset T$ is a finite $R$-module, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. It is a domain as a subring of $L$. Its fraction field is $L$: it contains $K$ and $x_i=y_i/a_i$, hence the whole $K$-linear span of this basis.

source.place: Lemma 1.2, printed p.104, finite subalgebra B with fraction field L; explicit scaled-basis construction. Supporting finiteness is the cited Mathlib leaf, and Noetherian permanence is Stacks Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: The ring $T$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $L$. Indeed, every element of $T$ satisfies a monic equation over $R\subset B$. Conversely let $E$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $L$. The inclusion $B\subset T$ makes $B$ integral over $R$, and $E$ is integral over $B$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] makes every element of $E$ integral over $R$, so $E\subset T$. Apply [lem-trf-normalization-integral-closure-krull] to the Noetherian domain $B$ with its own fraction field $L$: it gives that $T$ is a Krull domain, without presupposing that $T$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Lemma 1.2, printed p.104: A′ is the normalization of the finite subalgebra B and is a Krull domain. Integrality transitivity: Stacks Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive).

proof.text: Let $P\subset T$ be any height-one prime and put $q=P\cap R$. This is a prime of $R$, and it is nonzero. To see the latter directly, choose $0\ne z\in P$. Among monic equations for $z$ over $R$ choose one of least positive degree $m$. Its constant coefficient $r_0$ is nonzero: otherwise cancellation of $z\ne0$ in the field $L$ gives a monic equation of smaller degree (degree zero would say $1=0$). The equation shows $r_0=-z(z^{m-1}+r_{m-1}z^{m-2}+\cdots+r_1)\in P\cap R$. Thus the hypothesis applies to $R/q$, which is Japanese.

source.place: Lemma 1.2, printed p.104, nonzero contraction; the integral equation argument is written out. The stronger all-nonzero-primes hypothesis is exactly that used in Proposition 2.3, printed p.107, so the associated-prime detour is unnecessary.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-almost-finite-residue-field-degree] with base $R$, field extension $L/K$, subring $C=T$, and prime $P$. It gives that $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T/P)$ is finite over $k=\operatorname{Frac}(R/q)$. By [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], the integral closure $U$ of $R/q$ in $F$ is finite over $R/q$. There is an injective $R/q$-linear map $T/P\hookrightarrow U$: the domain $T/P$ embeds in its fraction field, and reduction modulo $P$ of each monic equation over $R$ shows its elements are integral over $R/q$, as defined in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The ring $R/q$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] applied to $R\twoheadrightarrow R/q$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $T/P$ finite over $R/q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes it a Noetherian ring.

source.place: Lemma 1.1, printed p.104: finite residue fraction-field degree (Nagata 33.10) and embedding in the finite integral closure. Supporting Stacks Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic).

proof.text: Step 2 proves that $T$ is Krull, and Steps 3–4 prove that $T/P$ is Noetherian for every height-one prime $P$ of $T$. Apply [lem-per-krull-height-one-quotients-noetherian] to $T$ to conclude that $T$ is a Noetherian ring. This is the asserted conclusion for the arbitrary finite extension $L/K$ fixed at the start.

source.place: Lemma 1.2, printed p.104, height-one quotient criterion and footnote (1).

proof_origin.place: Explicit assembly following Marot Lemmas 1.1–1.2, printed pp.104–105, and the all-nonzero-primes application in Proposition 2.3, printed p.107. Read online; local document WANTED in report. The stronger hypothesis removes the need for the associated-prime contraction argument.

SMF 103, 1975), printed pp.104-106. Lemma 1.2's route matches the delivery: a finite model B, Mori-Nagata (thm 4 of [5]), reduction to height-one quotients, then Lemma 1.1 via Nagata 33.10. Footnote (1) is exactly the new node: Nishimura's theorem that a Krull domain with Noetherian height-one quotients is Noetherian. The new node is self-contained, uses the same Krull definition as the existing trf Krull nodes, has no proof, and checks out on a field, Z and k[x1,x2,...] (hypothesis fails there). It is strictly more general than the item, so not a restatement, and the DAG and Mathlib have no duplicate. Step checks: (1) the scaled-basis monic equations are correct; B is finite and Noetherian with Frac B = L, and no separability is used. (2) T is the integral closure of B in L by transitivity, and Mori-Nagata is applied to B in its own fraction field. (3) A least-degree monic equation gives a nonzero constant term in P∩R, so q is nonzero. (4) The residue-degree node applies to C=T with no finiteness needed, then N-2 for R/q gives U finite, T/P sits inside U, and T/P is finite and Noetherian. (5) Assembly by the new node. Every cited statement says what is used.
